findings.title: BundleOptions.deinit will try to free `&config.features`, a field embedded in the config struct.
findings.body: After this change `transpiler.options.bundler_feature_flags` points at `config.features`. That set lives inside `JSBundler.Config`; it was never allocated with `allocator.create`. The new `BundleOptions.deinit` frees any pointer that is not the static empty set. It calls `.deinit()` on it and then `allocator.destroy(...)`. So if this transpiler's options are ever deinitialised, it destroys an interior pointer, which is undefined behaviour or a crash. `Config.deinit` also calls `self.features.deinit()`, so the set is freed twice. I could not see whether this transpiler's `deinit` runs on the JS API path. Fix: store ownership explicitly, e.g. an `owns_bundler_feature_flags` bool, or copy the set into a heap allocation owned by the options.

findings.title: The runtime transpiler cache key does not include the feature flags, so `bun run --feature` can get stale output.
findings.body: `bundler_feature_flags` changes the transpiled output, but it is not in `hash_fields_for_runtime_transpiler`, and nothing else shown hashes the flag set. Trigger: run a file large enough to be cached, first without `--feature=X`. Then `bun run --feature=X` (or `bun test --feature=X`) can load the cached transpilation where `feature("X")` was already replaced with `false`, and the reverse also happens. Fix: hash the sorted flag names into the cache key, or turn the runtime transpiler cache off when the flag set is not empty.

findings.title: Default and namespace imports from "bun:bundle" are removed silently and leave unbound identifiers.
findings.body: For `bun:bundle`, the statement is always replaced with `S.Empty`. Only named items are inspected. `import * as bundle from "bun:bundle"` and `import b from "bun:bundle"` are dropped with no error or warning, and their bindings are never declared. So `bundle.feature("X")` compiles to a reference to an undeclared global and throws a ReferenceError at runtime. Unknown named specifiers have the same problem: the warning says they "will be undefined", but they are never declared either, so using them also throws a ReferenceError. Fix: report an error when `stmt.star_name_loc` or `stmt.default_name` is set, and report an error (not a warning) for unknown specifiers, or declare them and bind them to `undefined`.
